skill.name: bigquery
skill.description: Guides authenticated BigQuery users through bq commands for schema inspection, row counts, table metadata, cautious sampling, and dbt validation.
skill.summary: Inspect BigQuery schemas, metadata, and row counts with data sensitivity safeguards.
skill.author: BfdCampos

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown or SQL backticks, not Ruby shell execution. Two temp-file writes are real medium-risk examples, and semantic review found high-risk organization-specific BigQuery access guidance involving named sensitive projects.

remediation.issue: Organization-specific project and dataset names are embedded in a public skill.
remediation.suggestion: Replace company-specific BigQuery project names with placeholders, or distribute the skill only inside the authorized organization.

remediation.issue: Sampling and export examples can expose sensitive warehouse data if classification is wrong.
remediation.suggestion: Remove SELECT * and broad export examples, or require explicit approval and dry-run checks before any row-level query.

remediation.issue: Schema output is written to a predictable /tmp/columns.txt path.
remediation.suggestion: Use a user-approved destination or a secure temporary file, and avoid writing metadata unless it is needed.

remediation.issue: External BigQuery CLI examples can run against real projects and incur costs.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands require user confirmation, least-privilege credentials, and cost checks before execution.

content.value_statement: BigQuery exploration can expose sensitive rows or create expensive scans. This skill guides metadata-first CLI checks, row counts, schema exports, and cautious sampling.
actual_capabilities: Shows bq query commands with explicit project IDs and Standard SQL.
Provides INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries for columns, tables, and metadata.
Shows row count checks without selecting table contents.
Documents output formats such as CSV, JSON, pretty JSON, and quiet mode.
Lists data sensitivity rules for PII, staff, authentication, and financial data.
Connects BigQuery checks to dbt source validation workflows.
limitations: Assumes access to specific BigQuery projects and datasets.
Does not authenticate users or enforce BigQuery permissions.
Cannot classify every table as sensitive before a query runs.
Command examples may incur cost if users run them against large tables.

use_cases.title: Inspect Source Schemas
use_cases.description: Review column names, types, nullability, and table metadata before writing analytics queries.

use_cases.title: Validate dbt Inputs
use_cases.description: Check source table existence and schema shape before creating or debugging dbt models.

use_cases.title: Review Sensitive Data Access
use_cases.description: Plan metadata-only checks and approval steps before querying restricted warehouse tables.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect the schema for PROJECT.DATASET.TABLE. Use INFORMATION_SCHEMA only and avoid table contents.

prompt_templates.title: Check Table Availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to confirm whether PROJECT.DATASET.TABLE exists, count its rows, and summarize available table metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare dbt Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare expected dbt source columns with BigQuery metadata for PROJECT.DATASET.TABLE.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Restricted Investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a safe BigQuery investigation for a sensitive dataset. Start with metadata, counts, and dry runs, then identify approval points before any sampling.

output_examples.input: Inspect the schema for a transactions table without reading customer data.
output_examples.output: A metadata-only plan that lists columns, data types, nullability, and table existence checks before any content query.

output_examples.input: Debug why a dbt model cannot find a source table.
output_examples.output: A sequence of BigQuery checks for project selection, dataset table listing, row counts, and schema comparison.

output_examples.input: Investigate a possible sensitive table mismatch.
output_examples.output: A guarded workflow that uses INFORMATION_SCHEMA first, asks for authorization before sampling, and avoids local PII exports.

best_practices: Start with INFORMATION_SCHEMA before any content query.
Use explicit project IDs and Standard SQL for every command.
Ask for authorization before sampling rows from sensitive datasets.
anti_patterns: Running broad content queries on PII, staff, authentication, or financial tables.
Exporting sensitive query results to local files.
Treating metadata access as approval for row-level data access.

faq.question: Does this skill run BigQuery commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command patterns that an agent or user may apply after checking access and intent.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive data?
faq.answer: It emphasizes metadata and row counts first, but users must still enforce permissions and approval rules.

faq.question: Can it help with dbt work?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes checks for source schemas, table existence, and column type validation before dbt runs.

faq.question: What BigQuery SQL mode does it use?
faq.answer: It recommends Standard SQL by using the BigQuery CLI legacy SQL disable flag.

faq.question: Does it manage Google Cloud authentication?
faq.answer: No. Authentication, project access, and billing controls must already be configured outside the skill.

faq.question: Can it export query results?
faq.answer: It includes export examples, but sensitive results should not be written to local files.
